key_insight: Scale-driven averaging attenuates variability in panel ultimate load, but spatially correlated interface properties remain essential for predicting early damage initiation and location.
engineering_relevance: Match stochastic model fidelity to the design criterion: spatially uniform variability for global load capacity and correlated random fields for local skin–stringer bond integrity.
method: Extend likelihood-free Bayesian calibration to Mode II interface properties using experimental coupon data.
Propagate interface variability from coupons to aerospace panels with simulation-based stochastic finite elements.
Compare industrial B-basis, spatially uniform variability, and spatially correlated random-field strategies.
evidence_signal: Coupon experiments support stochastic parameter calibration, while panel simulations show uncertainty attenuation in ultimate load and weak-spot-driven early damage.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative accuracy metrics or panel-scale experimental validation, leaving predictive transfer across scales to be verified.
paper_title: Scaling of Interface Variability in Aerospace Composite Structures: A Multi-scale Stochastic Approach from Local Identification to Panel Response
